title: A Shipwreck That May Be the World's Oldest
summary:
Archaeologists may have found the world's oldest shipwreck. Based on clues from its cargo, including pottery, a research team has tentatively dated the wreck to around 2700-2400 BCE. But much work remains, and no paper has been published in a peer-reviewed journal yet.

Associate Professor Hakan Öniz of Akdeniz University, Antalya, found the wreck in shallow waters off Kekova, west of Antalya in Turkey, in 2024. He followed clues from local seafarers.

Nothing is left of the ship. What remains is its cargo, stuck in the rocky slope along the Kekova coast. The ship now rests on the seabed between two islands. The team thinks it likely hid in calmer lee waters during a storm while sailing along the coast of southern Turkey.

Over the past four months, divers pulled pottery from barnacles on the rocky underwater slope. The cargo included large ceramic storage jars called amphorae, which once held products from the eastern Mediterranean.

If the dating is right, the find could change what we know about ancient Mediterranean connections during the Early Bronze Age, around 4,500 years ago.
why_it_matters: It is like finding an old storage jar under the sea that can tell you what people carried and traded long before you were born.
